World War II - Major Events and Timeline

Introduction

World War II (1939-1945) was the deadliest conflict in human history, involving most of the world's nations organized into two opposing military alliances: the Allies and the Axis powers. The war resulted in an estimated 70-85 million fatalities.

Causes of World War II

1. Treaty of Versailles (1919)
   - Imposed harsh penalties on Germany after WWI
   - Created economic hardship and resentment
   - Territorial losses and military restrictions

2. Rise of Totalitarian Regimes
   - Fascism in Italy under Mussolini (1922)
   - Nazism in Germany under Hitler (1933)
   - Militarism in Japan

3. Policy of Appeasement
   - European powers tried to avoid war by conceding to Hitler's demands
   - Munich Agreement (1938) allowed Germany to annex Sudetenland
   - Emboldened aggressive expansion

4. Economic Depression
   - Global economic crisis of the 1930s
   - Created instability and desperation
   - Made populations susceptible to extremist ideologies

Major Events Timeline

1939 - War Begins
- September 1: Germany invades Poland
- September 3: Britain and France declare war on Germany
- September 17: Soviet Union invades Poland from the east

1940 - Axis Expansion
- April-June: Germany conquers Denmark, Norway, Belgium, Netherlands, and France
- June 22: France signs armistice with Germany
- July-October: Battle of Britain - German air campaign against Britain
- September: Tripartite Pact signed (Germany, Italy, Japan)

1941 - Global War
- June 22: Operation Barbarossa - Germany invades Soviet Union
- December 7: Japan attacks Pearl Harbor
- December 8: United States declares war on Japan
- December 11: Germany and Italy declare war on United States

1942 - Turning Point
- June: Battle of Midway - decisive U.S. naval victory over Japan
- August 1942-February 1943: Battle of Stalingrad - Soviet victory, turning point in Eastern Front
- October-November: Battle of El Alamein - British victory in North Africa

1943 - Allied Momentum
- February: German forces surrender at Stalingrad
- July: Allies invade Sicily
- September: Italy surrenders; German forces occupy northern Italy
- November: Tehran Conference (Roosevelt, Churchill, Stalin)

1944 - Liberation Begins
- June 6: D-Day - Allied invasion of Normandy, France
- August: Paris liberated
- December: Battle of the Bulge - Germany's last major offensive in the West

1945 - End of the War
- January: Soviet forces liberate Auschwitz concentration camp
- February: Yalta Conference
- April 12: President Roosevelt dies; Truman becomes president
- April 30: Hitler commits suicide in Berlin
- May 8: V-E Day - Germany surrenders unconditionally
- August 6: Atomic bomb dropped on Hiroshima
- August 9: Atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki
- August 15: V-J Day - Japan announces surrender
- September 2: Japan formally surrenders aboard USS Missouri

Key Theaters of War

European Theater
- Western Front: France, Belgium, Netherlands, Germany
- Eastern Front: Soviet Union - largest and bloodiest theater
- Mediterranean: North Africa, Italy
- Strategic bombing campaign against Germany

Pacific Theater
- Island-hopping campaign across Pacific islands
- Burma Campaign
- China-Burma-India Theater
- Naval warfare dominated by aircraft carriers

The Holocaust

- Systematic genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany
- Approximately 6 million Jews murdered
- Also targeted: Roma, disabled people, political opponents, homosexuals, Soviet POWs
- Concentration camps and extermination camps
- Liberation of camps revealed the full horror in 1945

Consequences and Legacy

1. Human Cost
   - 70-85 million deaths (3% of world population)
   - Millions of refugees and displaced persons
   - Devastation of cities and infrastructure

2. Political Changes
   - United Nations established (1945)
   - Division of Germany and Berlin
   - Beginning of the Cold War
   - Decolonization movements accelerated

3. Technological Advances
   - Nuclear weapons
   - Radar and jet aircraft
   - Computers (codebreaking)
   - Antibiotics (penicillin)

4. Economic Impact
   - Marshall Plan for European reconstruction
   - United States emerged as economic superpower
   - Bretton Woods system established

5. Legal and Moral Framework
   - Nuremberg Trials (1945-1946)
   - Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
   - Geneva Conventions updated (1949)
   - Concept of "crimes against humanity"

The war fundamentally reshaped the international order and continues to influence global politics, international law, and collective memory today.
